properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-24 by Anthony — *"go with (c), distribute by function"* — after asking the question that forced it: **"are these components being taken from dynograph-foundation being added to an existing subsystem or a new subsystem?"**

Each absorbed piece joins the component that USES it. `dynograph-core`'s types land in `sys:foundation` beside `cmp:schema` and `cmp:nodes` because that is what they are; the graph algorithms join the graph component; the storage engine joins `sys:store`. **No `sys:absorbed-foundation` is created.**

═══ WHY NOT A DEDICATED SUBSYSTEM ═══

It was the obvious alternative and it is the wrong one: a subsystem for absorbed code would **rebuild in the model the very boundary the absorption removes**. The point of absorbing is that there is no supplier any more. Keeping a labelled block of "their code" preserves a seam that has stopped existing, and every later reader would have to be told it means "historically foreign" rather than "architecturally separate".

Provenance does not need a subsystem to survive. It lives in the file headers (tag, commit, file, what was taken, what was not) and in each increment's ChangeEvent, so **"what came from outside?" stays answerable without a structural marker**.

═══ ⭐⭐ THIS RESOLVES `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier`, AND BY HIS OWN EARLIER ARGUMENT ═══

That node has been open since 2026-08-17 with three options: A leave it a supplier (what the design says today), B add it as a ninth black box, C complete the supplier treatment.

**The answer is none of them, because absorption dissolves the question.** And the way it dissolves is the interesting part:

Option B was rejected on a specific ground — *"a subsystem you do not build, cannot change, and release separately is not a subsystem — modelling it as one asserts ownership reflow2 does not have."* **Absorption removes all three objections at once.** After it, reflow2 DOES build it, CAN change it, and does NOT release it separately. The objection was never to the idea; it was to the ownership, and the ownership is what changed.

And his motivation on that node is the strongest argument for distributing rather than fencing: *"I wanted graph theory to undergird everything ... graph theory was important to my concept of reflow2."* **Something that undergirds everything is not a box beside everything.** Option (c) puts it where he said it belonged a week before this decision was taken.

⚠️ Option C's finding SURVIVES and is not closed by this: the design's picture of its supplier is partial — `dynograph-text` is consumed transitively with no interface node, and "what does the foundation offer that we do not take?" is unanswerable from the graph. For the crates being absorbed that stops mattering. For anything left external it still does.

═══ 🛑 THE CONDITION ON INCREMENTS 3-5, from his other question ═══

He also asked: *"I'd imagine in adding these, we are building capabilities/functions that have no requirements in reflow2?"* **Correct, and it is a real hazard from increment 3 onward.**

Today those behaviours are modelled as `ifc:req-dyno-*` at `designation: required` — which is a legitimate way to have no requirement: reflow2 is not claiming to DO the thing, it is claiming to NEED it. Absorption deletes that framing. Nothing would then say why reflow2 stores in RocksDB or detects communities with Leiden.

⇒ **WRITING THE REQUIREMENT IS PART OF THE INCREMENT, NOT CLEANUP AFTER IT.** reflow2 has a detector for exactly this (`unmotivated_capability`), so the design will say so rather than anyone having to remember — but a gap raised after the code lands is a gap raised late.

⭐ INCREMENT 1 IS CLEAN AND THAT IS WHY IT WENT FIRST: `stats.rs` is implementation beneath `cap:dimensions`, which already SATISFIES `req:coherence`. No new capability, no new requirement owed. It also got NO component of its own — 35 lines of arithmetic do not earn one, and minting `cmp:stats` would be the over-engineering this project watches for.

═══ ⚠️ THE SNAG THIS ORDER WALKS INTO ═══

`cmp:graph` exists in BOTH designs for different things — reflow2's graph module and dynograph's graph crate. It is one of the three id collisions that would have blocked the mirror. **Increment 3 needs a distinct component name for the absorbed algorithms**, decided before the code moves rather than discovered while moving it.
properties.name: DECIDED — absorbed foundation code is distributed BY FUNCTION into the components that use it, and no "absorbed" subsystem is created
properties.rationale:
Recorded separately from the absorption plan because it answers a MODELLING question rather than a scoping one, and because it settles a decision open for a week on grounds that node could not have reached: it weighed where the boundary should sit while the supplier existed, and this changes whether there is a supplier.

⭐ THE PATTERN WORTH KEEPING: an option rejected for a reason can become correct when the reason stops holding, and nothing re-examines it automatically. Option B was rejected because reflow2 did not own the code. Nobody would have re-read that node on the day the ownership changed — it surfaced only because Anthony asked where the absorbed components go. **A rejection carries its ground; when the ground moves the rejection is worth re-reading, and no mechanism does that.**
